sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin & Introduction**: Introduced in India in 1994-95 under the recommendations of the **Chelliah Committee** on Tax Reforms, initially covering only 3 services.
• **Constitutional Validity**: Initially enacted under the residuary powers of Parliament (Article 248 read with Entry 97 of List I). Later, the **88th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** inserted **Article 268A** to explicitly provide for the levy of service tax by the Union and appropriation of proceeds by Union and States.
• **Negative List Regime**: Introduced in 2012 (Finance Act, 2012), shifting from a positive list of taxable services to a comprehensive **Negative List** where all services except those specifically exempted or listed in the negative list were taxable.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Subsumed into the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** on July 1, 2017, eliminating cascading effects and multiple indirect tax layers.

items.definition: Set of rules determining the exact time when a service is deemed to have been provided for the purpose of payment of service tax.

items.term: Place of Provision of Services Rules
items.definition: Rules used to determine whether a service is provided within taxable territory of India, critical for cross-border transactions and export/import of services.
A mechanism where the liability to pay tax is cast on the recipient of the service rather than the supplier, used to plug leakage from unorganized service providers.
Tax Reforms Committee that recommended the introduction of Service Tax as part of the broader structural economic reforms post-1991 balance of payments crisis.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Urban Service Clusters**: Metropolitan cities like Bengaluru, Mumbai, NCR (Delhi), Hyderabad, and Chennai accounted for the vast majority of service tax collections due to concentration of IT/ITeS, financial services, and corporate headquarters.
• **Disparities**: Led to inter-state fiscal imbalances as origin-based service taxation benefited service-originating states over consuming states, prompting the shift to destination-based GST.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Complex classification disputes, valuation issues on composite works contracts, double taxation of software (goods vs. services), and high compliance costs.
• **Policy Interventions**: Introduction of Swachh Bharat Cess (0.5%), Krishi Kalyan Cess (0.5%), and ultimately the historic transition to GST to ensure seamless Input Tax Credit (ITC).

items.title: Mnemonic for Evolution Milestones
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'C N G' (Chelliah -> Negative List -> GST)
• **Decoded Meaning**: C = Chelliah Committee (1994 launch), N = Negative List (2012 overhaul), G = GST (2017 subsumption).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the chronological order of major service tax milestones.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Service tax was an Union List subject (Residuary Entry 97 / Article 248), administered by the Central Board of Excise and Customs (CBEC), unlike Sales Tax/VAT which was a State List subject.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently poses statements claiming that Service Tax was levied by States under the State List or concurrently under the Concurrent List before GST. Remember: Service Tax was exclusively a Central levy (Union List / Residuary powers).

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 (Indian Economy & Mobilization of Resources), analyze how the transition from Service Tax to GST resolved the vexed 'goods vs. services' classification litigation (e.g., software licenses, packaged food) and enhanced the tax-to-GDP ratio.

keyTakeaways: Service Tax was introduced in 1994 on the recommendation of the Chelliah Committee and was an exclusive Central indirect tax.
The 2012 'Negative List' regime revolutionized service taxation by making all services taxable except those explicitly exempted.
Service Tax, along with Central Excise and State VAT, was subsumed under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in July 2017, establishing a unified destination-based tax system.
